editorialNotes.basis: Hyman, Vol. 3, p. 1071 (right column). The רבה בר איסי entry ends "ואולי הוא" ("and perhaps he is") with no complement. The next printed heading, "רבה בר איתי", is the only heading on the page without a closing period, and its text opens with the relative "שהיה" ("who was"), then returns to Sotah 30a, the one citation in the רבה בר איסי entry. Hebrew Wikisource's editor footnotes the same place: "המשך המשפט בערך הבא". Read together: "perhaps he is Rabba bar Itai, who was in Rav's time (see Rava bar Itai); and in Sotah 30a too read 'Rabba bar Itai', and this needs investigation (וצ״ע)". Hyman's identification is tentative. The bracketed words are printed under the heading רבה בר איתי, which remains its own entry.
